speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood work (CBC, ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid Factor, CCP) not available in current data; NORMAL READINGS. X-ray of right hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint and the resting extension strongly suggest a tendon rupture or severe tenosynovitis. Have you experienced any recent trauma to that finger, or do you see any signs of infection like redness or warmth? REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound of right hand flexor tendons.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound of right hand flexor tendons not available in current data; NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Trigger Finger (Stenosing Tenosynovitis) of the right ring finger.

The normal ultrasound rules out a complete tendon rupture, and your specific symptoms of locking at the distal interphalangeal joint with resting extension are classic for a tendon catching in its sheath. The inability to flex suggests the tendon is stuck in a flexed position rather than extended.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
